dataset_name: LearnSphere AI Prototype Sample Learning Content
purpose: Standalone example content matching the prototype's embedded supervised-learning lesson and quiz. This is educational demo content, not an ML training corpus or production user data.
source_note: Adapted from the sample lesson and quiz embedded in LearnSphere/src/App.tsx in the supplied archive.

lessons.title: Supervised Learning Basics
lessons.summary: Supervised learning trains a model from labelled examples. Classification predicts a category, while regression predicts a numeric value. A separate test set estimates performance on examples not used for training.

transcript.text: Supervised learning uses examples paired with the correct answer, called a label.
Features describe an example. The label is the target a model learns to predict.
Classification predicts a category, such as whether an email is spam.
Regression predicts a numeric value, such as a house price.
Training examples are used to fit the model's parameters.
A separate test set checks how well the trained model generalises to unseen examples.
Keep evaluation examples separate from training examples to get a more useful estimate of performance.

lessons.title: Neural Networks Explained
lessons.summary: Neural networks combine layers of connected units. During training, weights and biases are adjusted to reduce prediction error.

transcript.text: A neural network passes input through connected layers of computational units.
Weights control connection strength; biases shift a unit's activation.
Training adjusts weights and biases to reduce prediction error.

lessons.title: Gradient Descent and Learning
lessons.summary: Gradient descent minimises a loss function by updating parameters in the direction that reduces loss. The learning rate controls update size.

transcript.text: A loss function measures how far predictions are from desired outputs.
Gradient descent moves opposite the gradient to reduce the loss.
The learning rate sets each update size and affects training stability.

lessons.title: Backpropagation Intuition
lessons.summary: Backpropagation applies the chain rule to calculate how model parameters contribute to loss, allowing an optimiser to update them.

transcript.text: Backpropagation efficiently computes parameter gradients in a neural network.
The chain rule connects derivatives across layers so loss gradients can flow backward.
An optimiser uses computed gradients to update weights and biases.

questions.question: Which type of learning uses labelled training data?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses input examples paired with known labels or target values.

questions.question: Predicting a house price is usually which kind of task?
questions.explanation: House price is a numeric value, so this is a regression task.

questions.question: Why is a separate test set useful?
options: It increases the number of training labels
It estimates performance on unseen examples
It removes the need to train a model
questions.explanation: A held-out test set provides an estimate of how well a trained model generalises to unseen data.
